newsitem.title: USA: Investors on edge after market's strong 1st half.
newsitem.headline: Investors on edge after market's strong 1st half.

text.p: After ending the second-quarter on a rollercoaster ride, Wall Street faces a rough road next week as Federal Reserve policy-makers and a slew of economic data determine the course of interest rates in the third quarter.

Pumped up by a 19 percent first half gain, the Dow Jones industrial average begins the second half of the year with the market looking for confirmation from new economic data that the Fed will not be inclined to raise rates again.
"The market is struggling now. Its important that the numbers say to us that the economy remains soft," said Hugh Johnson chief investment officer at First Albany.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 33.47 points to 7,687.72 Friday but finished with a loss of 108.79 points for the week.

Investors will take their cues from the release of economic statistics including the purchasing managers' report for June and car and truck sales on Tuesday and the June jobs report on Thursday. Friday is the July 4th holiday.

Attention will also turn to the meeting of Fed policy-makers on Tuesday and Wednesday. Although the central bankers are not expected to raise rates next week investors are already worried about moves later this summer.
The Fed raised short-term rates in March, the first increase in more than two years, in a bid to ward off inflation. But it held rates steady last month.

Wall Street got a glimpse of the bad news bears on Monday when remarks by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto about possible sales of U.S. government securities sent stocks down more than 192 points in their second-worst decline ever.
Although Japan acted quickly to defuse his comments investors are jittery over U.S.-Japan economic relations.

"Interest rates in August will turn on the indicators that we see next week," said Johnson. "Secondly, creeping into the consciousness of investors is the deterioration of Japanese investments. None of this would be a problem if it didn't happen at a time when we've had a very big runup in a very short period of time.
The Dow Jones industrial average stood at about 7,204 in the last week in May and got as high as 7,868 last week -- a 664 point gain in a month.
"The market has given back some but it's been a humdinger of a month," Johnson said.
Upcoming corporate earnings reports and earnings forecasts for the third quarter could also give the market some jitters. "The focus will change in the second half," said Oppenheimer's Metz.
"If we maintain the gains we have made so far it will be a fabulous year," said Jonathan Dodd, a technical analyst at Smith Barney. "I expect us to end here or below."
"Stocks as an asset class are going to be under some pressure," said Gary Anderson of Anderson & Roe, an Oregon firm that advises portfolio managers.
Anderson said he expected stocks in the second half to be "ragged to down." He said investors who have been holding may be tempted to sell on any good news. "I expect a lot of volatility," he said.
On Friday, the Nasdaq composite index rose 1.77 points to 1,438.15, but it fell 8.95 for the week.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 3.62 to 887.30, but lost 11.40 for the week. The American Stock Exchange index added 3.97 to 620.07, but was down 3.2 points from last Friday.
The NYSE composite index of all listed common stocks rose 2.37 to 463.30 for a loss of 4.54 for the week.
